threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' and not 'the Overground'—big mistake! You'll hear locals drop the 'Tube' like it’s a holiday train.
Last night on the 77 bus, a guy serenaded the driver with classic soul tunes. Didn't have a clue he was belting it out. Only in Brixton!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I saw kids using the U-Bahn as their personal playground—jumping between carriages, giggling like it was a carnival ride.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: You can hop a U-Bahn and find a spontaneous street party on any Saturday night in Kreuzberg—where else can you find a club underground and above ground at the same time?

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know you're local when you can guess the BART delays by the time of day, yet still get annoyed when a stop is closed unexpectedly.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the bus serenading the passengers with an accordion. The whole ride turned from dreary to a spontaneous concert. Classic Tenderloin.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can grab a coffee and sit for hours; in Gràcia, locals down their café con leche and dash to work. It's a quick sip, not a long sit.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell when someone’s new if they’re still amazed by the 'free' tapas with drinks at the bars. The locals expect it, but fresh faces are always snapping selfies with their plates.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it’s called the Hackney Empire and not just 'The Empire.' Everyone around here just calls it 'The' like it’s on a first-name basis.
Caught a guy on the 77 singing to himself—never knew Fleetwood Mac could sound so haunting at 2 AM. Only in Brixton, I guess.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I saw a guy in a full suit haggling over a kebab at 3 AM, then shake hands with a hipster artist. That's Neukölln for you.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you find an entire beach bar in an old factory courtyard, complete with sand and palm trees, right next to a graffiti-covered wall.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a true local by how they don’t flinch at the BART delays, while newcomers are still checking their phones like it’ll change anything.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Heard a saxophonist jamming next to the 5 line stop, while a guy in a three-piece suit danced along. Just another day in the Tenderloin chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists flock to Parc Güell, but miss the quiet, vibrant life at Plaça de la Vila, where locals gossip over coffee on weekdays.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot a recent arrival by their over-excitement at ordering 'pan con tomate' like it’s the secret to life. Locals just nod.
